newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU AIDS SOUTH AFRICA'S APARTHEID TRUTH PROBE.
newsitem.headline: EU AIDS SOUTH AFRICA'S APARTHEID TRUTH PROBE.

text.p: The European Union said on Monday it would give South African Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu 10.7 million rand ($2.4 million) towards the work of his post-apartheid Truth and Reconciliation Commission.
The South African government has voted 70 million rand for the truth commission's two-year probe into the human rights record of the war over apartheid.

But Tutu and President Nelson Mandela have said they hope for significant foreign support to help expose the truth about the conflict, to pardon politically-motivated offenders and to compensate victims.
Truth Commission spokesman John Allen said the commission had so far received two million rand in direct aid and the services of several investigators seconded to South Africa by foreign governments.
He said a number of governments had made commitments, which had not yet been followed up.
The EU said in a statement the programme was part of its commitment to give South Africa about 600 million rand a year for the first five years of democracy, which bgean in 1994.
"The EU believes its assistance...will contribute to the successful completion of the enormous and complex task faced by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission," the statement said.
The money will be used to pay for additional investigators, for research and towards the cost of translation services.
